claims.text: An AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5 surface coating can be produced by laser cladding.
Introducing Ti into AlCoCrFeNi will trigger in situ formation of a stable, self-adaptive oxide film during sliding.
The oxide film acts as a lubricating barrier.
The oxide film reduces both coefficient of friction and wear rate over a wide temperature range.
Untreated AlCoCrFeNi lacks a continuous protective oxide film.
The AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5 formulation incorporates approximately 0.5 atom% Ti.
The intervention should remain effective in dry sliding from room temperature to approximately 900°C under atmospheric conditions.
AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5 has a refined multiphase microstructure.
The modified microstructure contains well-distributed Ti-rich regions.
Sliding rapidly converts the Ti-rich regions into a continuous protective oxide film.
Ti has sufficiently high oxygen affinity to drive oxide-layer formation in this alloy during sliding.
A thin, adherent oxide layer forms during sliding even at low temperatures.
The oxide layer limits direct metal-to-metal contact, thereby reducing friction and wear.
At elevated temperatures, a protective oxide layer forms on AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5 and increases wear resistance under atmospheric wear conditions.
At higher temperatures, the oxide remains stable and lubricating despite increased mechanical and thermal stresses.
The Ti-containing laser-cladded coating will reduce coefficient of friction by approximately 15–25% relative to untreated AlCoCrFeNi.
The Ti-containing coating will substantially reduce wear rate relative to untreated AlCoCrFeNi across the entire room-temperature-to-900°C range.
Prior untreated AlCoCrFeNi wear studies show that protective oxide films form only gradually or incompletely.
The benefit depends on an oxidative environment and may be lost in strongly reducing atmospheres.
Loads that exceed the coating's mechanical integrity may prevent proper oxide-film adhesion and limit the benefit.

contradictions.description: The intervention interprets Ti0.5 as approximately 0.5 atom% Ti. In standard AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5 compositional notation, Ti has a 0.5 molar ratio relative to 1 for each other element, corresponding to about 9.1 at% Ti, not 0.5 at%.

The hypothesis and predicted outcome assert effectiveness across the entire room-temperature-to-900°C range, while the uncertainty field states that robustness at lower temperatures still requires verification.
